title: X10TimezoneDedupKnownLimitationTests.differingTimeZoneDevicesBothFire is date/time-dependent and fails deterministically as of 2026-07-29

description: Discovered while running plan-5a's binding full-suite verification gate. The test asserts centerB.pendingNotificationRequests().isEmpty == false (device B's cross-timezone reminder should still be scheduled, just not deduped against device A's fire) but centerB has ZERO pending requests instead — a different failure mode than the known dedup limitation the suite documents. Confirmed via a temporary git worktree at commit 6cc5fa4c (tip of plan-4c, before any plan-5a work) that this test ALSO fails there, byte-identically — proving it predates plan-5a entirely and is not a regression from H5/M4/M6/M7/L3/L4/L5/X19/X20's fixes. Likely mechanism: the test computes deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(86_400) and each device's all-day fire instant from that using its own local calendar day + 9am; depending on the wall-clock time the suite runs at, Tokyo's computed fire instant for 'the same' deadline can already be in the past by the time NotificationScheduler.reconcile() runs, and the scheduler may correctly decline to schedule an already-past notification — zero pending requests, not a dedup match. This would make the test fail only during certain hours of the day (UTC-relative), which matches it failing consistently across two runs made minutes apart today but not necessarily on every date/time. Needs: (1) root-cause confirmation of the exact mechanism, (2) a fix that makes the test's fixture time-independent (e.g. anchor devAFireDate/devBFireDate relative to a fixed injected 'now' rather than the live Date()), not a change to production scheduling behavior. Filed for whichever plan owns Wave 6a's completeness sweep; not fixed in plan-5a to avoid conflating an unrelated pre-existing test fragility with this plan's own findings.
